_metadata: Plain-language HARD judge suite (plain_language_hard_v1, 3 passages). Each passage hides a trap the naive rewrite loses: a double condition plus an exception, a load-bearing distinction (effective date vs. notification date), and a double-negative registration rule. Scored by the LLM-as-judge against the reference using tasks/rubrics/plain_language_v1.yaml. Built to stress faithfulness/completeness the easy suite couldn't. Originals are illustrative Duke-flavored phrasings and references are hand-written PLACEHOLDER golds (not validated by a Duke communications/compliance office) — pipeline validation, not authoritative. New questions go in a new version file.

question: Rewrite this in plain language for a general student audience, keeping ALL conditions and exceptions: "Graduate students enrolled on at least a half-time basis are eligible for the transit subsidy, except those in receipt of a full tuition waiver, provided that the enrollment verification form is submitted on or before the census date."
reference: If you're a grad student enrolled at least half-time, you can get the transit subsidy — unless you're receiving a full tuition waiver, in which case you don't qualify. Either way, you have to turn in your enrollment verification form by the census date.

question: Rewrite this refund notice in plain language for students, keeping the distinction it draws: "Tuition refunds are prorated according to the effective date of withdrawal, which is determined by the date the withdrawal takes effect in the registrar's system, and not by the date on which the student provides notification of intent to withdraw."
reference: Your tuition refund is based on when your withdrawal officially takes effect in the registrar's system — not on the day you tell them you plan to withdraw. The refund is prorated (partial) based on that official effective date, so if the two dates differ, only the effective date counts.

question: Rewrite this registration rule in plain language, keeping the exception: "No student shall be permitted to register absent the satisfaction of all outstanding financial obligations, unless a formal deferral of said obligations has been approved by the Bursar's Office."
reference: You can't register until you've paid off everything you owe — unless the Bursar's Office has approved an official deferral (a formal delay) of what you owe. With an approved deferral, you can register even if the balance isn't cleared yet.
